title: Documentation and operational readiness
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of documentation and operational readiness
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: Instructions for operating and recovering a service
A defined observation of service state
The actor responsible for ongoing decisions

blocks.text: Runbook says start server, but omits data version and recovery steps. Another operator cannot reproduce a result.
Add exact configuration/version references, fixture setup, verification and recovery. Do not publish secret values to make setup easier.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Add exact configuration/version references, fixture setup, verification and recovery. Do not publish secret values to make setup easier.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Documentation includes all setup steps but no incident owner or compatible rollback. Identify readiness gaps.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Specify escalation owner, fallback and tested rollback dependencies. A setup-only guide does not cover operation.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Documentation readiness requires a tested replay and operational ownership, not merely complete-looking prose.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
